podcast.title: Annette Beard's Departure
podcast.body: Annette Beard left the group after two Holland-Dozier-Holland records ("Heat Wave" and "Quicksand") and two subsequent singles failed to break the top 40. She was replaced by Betty Kelly. "a net left, being replaced by Betty Kelly."

podcast.title: Backing Vocalists for Marvin Gaye
podcast.body: The Van Dellers became Marvin Gaye's backing vocalists, both in the studio and for shows like the Motortown Revue. This gave them early exposure and allowed them to perform with many other artists. "Van Dellers were now also Marvin Gaye's backing vocalists, and it shows like the Muggeda Town review shows, as well as performing their own set, the Van Dellers would sing with Gaye as well."

podcast.title: Classic Lineup Members Still Alive
podcast.body: Martha and the Van Dellers are noted as one of the very few 1960s hitmaking groups where all members of their classic lineup (Martha, Rosalind, Betty, Annette, and Lois) are still alive and performing, despite Gloria Williams' death in 2000. "Martha and the Van Della's are one of the very few 60s hitmaking groups, where all the members of their classic lineup are still alive and performing."

podcast.title: Gloria Williams' Departure
podcast.body: Gloria Williams left the group around the time "I'll Have to Let Him Go" was released, after Martha Reeves became the definitive leader. Reasons suggested include Gloria's disapproval of Martha's leadership or her desire to keep a stable job with the city rather than risk it for a full-time singing career. "That was released under the Martha and the Van Dulles name, and around this point, Gloria left the group."

podcast.title: Greatest Motown Girl Group
podcast.body: The Van Dellers are recognized as one of the greatest Motown acts and girl groups, with their biggest hits standing up against any contemporary Motown recordings, still embodying "the Sound of Young America" nearly 60 years later. "The Van Della's were one of the greatest of the Motown acts, and one of the greatest of the girl groups, and their biggest hits stand up against anything that any of the other Motown acts were doing at the time."

podcast.title: Name Origin
podcast.body: After being signed to Motown, Barry Gordy wanted a new name for The Delphiys. They first went by The Dominettes. Martha Reeves then suggested "Martha and the Van Dellers," combining Van Dyke Street (where she lived) and Della Reese (her favorite singer). Rosalind Ashford disputes Martha's role in naming, stating the group was initially just "The Van Dellers" with Gloria as lead. "Martha suggested a name based on the street she lived on, Van Dyke Street, and Delerie's Martha's favourite singer, who had hits like, what do you know? The group became Martha and the Van Dellers."

podcast.title: Post-Motown Split and Touring Groups
podcast.body: When Motown moved from Detroit to LA in the early 1970s, Martha Reeves chose not to relocate, leading to the group's split. Currently, there are two touring versions: "Martha Reeves and the Van Dellers" (Martha and her sisters, including Lois Reeves) and "The Original Van Dellers" (Rosalind Ashford and Annette Beard). "When Motown moved from Detroit to LA in the early 70s, Martha was one of those who decided not to make the move with the label, and the groups split up"

podcast.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction
podcast.body: The classic lineup members Martha Reeves, Rosalind Ashford, Betty Kelly, Annette Beard, and Lois Reeves were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1995, marking them as only the second all-female group to receive this honor. "Martha, Rosalind, Betty, Annette and Lois were all also inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1995, becoming only the second all-female group to be inducted."

podcast.title: Shift in Group Leadership
podcast.body: The session for "I'll Have to Let Him Go" marked a turning point where Martha Reeves definitively took over as the leader of the group, leading to Gloria Williams' departure. This shift in power dynamics might have been influenced by Martha booking the group for sessions as Mickey Stevenson's secretary. "this seems to be the moment that Martha Reeves took over the group."
